title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
summary: Hold: the governance table supplies a read-only Graph listing operation where administrators need an operation that changes spending controls. The rollout and licensing statements are supported; two dashboard descriptions also need qualifications because Microsoft's comparison and monitoring articles differ.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to make usage-based billing models accessible from the Chat model selector.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: The roadmap says tenant administrators need to provide credits for users to interact with these models.
claims.quote: Tenant admins will need to allocate credits so that users can interact with these models.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans credit requests to tenant administrators after users consume their allotted credits.
claims.quote: If users consume their allotted credits, they will be able to request credits from their tenant admins.

claims.claim: The notice names Claude Fable 5.1 as a generally available UBB model with this rollout.

claims.claim: In-product requests for additional credits are planned after the initial rollout.
claims.quote: After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.

claims.claim: The notice gives no date for the subsequent in-product credit-request rollout.

claims.claim: The USL provides the fixed-price foundation for everyday AI.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.

claims.claim: UBB covers advanced AI and frontier models beyond everyday AI included in the USL.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and cost; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: UBB model usage is consumption-billed in Copilot Credits, supporting the consumption licensing model and variable cost rating.
claims.quote: UBB is used in Copilot for capabilities such as Cowork, Code, Autopilot, new agentic experiences in SharePoint, or when working with newer agentic frontier models such as Astra and Fable. UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot USL is required in addition to UBB enablement and credits.
claims.quote: Verify that users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL).- Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models.- Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.

claims.claim: Administrators must set up a billing policy before users can use AI experiences requiring UBB.
claims.quote: Admins must set up a billing policy before a user can use AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The feature's default state is admin-opt-in because administrators must enable UBB and provide credits.
claims.quote: To provide users with access to UBB models: ... Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models.- Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.

claims.claim: Learn does not publish per-model Chat credit rates for GPT-6 Astra or Claude Fable 5.1 in the material checked.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center already provides identity-based spending policies in Copilot Cost Management.
claims.quote: Add Identity-based spending policy ... In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies control access and spending limits rather than reserving or allocating credits to users or groups.
claims.quote: Spending policies only define access and spending limits, not credit allocation. ... Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Identity-based policies scope access by users or groups, with individual users currently targeted through security groups.
claims.quote: Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service. ... At this time, you can only support specific users and resource accounts through security groups.

claims.claim: A user moving between Entra ID groups takes on the new group's policy while retaining consumption history.
claims.quote: If a user moves from one Microsoft Entra ID group to another during a billing period, the new group's spending policy becomes effective for the user. However, the user's consumption history carries forward across the policy change.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can configure monthly policy-level credit spending limits.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure per-user monthly spending limits.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.claim: The management article says users reaching a spending limit lose access for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Spending policies support alerts at administrator-configured usage thresholds.
claims.quote: Specify the usage threshold for the policy. ... Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.claim: The monitoring article allows a running task to finish after exceeding a per-user limit in a group policy.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select and change billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: The setup article says AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit policies and manage limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.claim: The setup article says AI administrator and License administrator roles cannot create spending policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The setup article inconsistently also includes License Administrator among read-only roles.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: Spending-policy configuration is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies is the automation supplied for the row governing usage-based billing, spending policies, limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Get a list of spendingPolicy objects. ... Don't supply a request body for this method.
claims.fix: The GET exists but cannot be the configuration equivalent, even with its read-only disclaimer. Replace controls[0].api.call with 'PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}' and its docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-update. Replace the row note and the matching Graph paragraph with: 'The request body sets periodLimit and perUserLimit for policy and per-user monthly limits; this call does not configure alerts. Beta APIs can change and are unsupported in production.' Keep the row's broader UI coverage; do not imply this one call configures every setting in that UI.

claims.claim: The currently printed GET only lists policies and does not change limits or alerts.
claims.quote: Get a list of spendingPolicy objects. ... Read service settings, alert settings, recipients, and group assignments on their dedicated endpoints.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The access-request control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Settings > All Settings. ... Select Access to usage-based billing experiences.

claims.claim: No API equivalent was found for controlling who may request access to UBB experiences.
claims.quote: Searched Learn: 'Access to usage-based billing experiences API', 'request spending policy Graph access setting'. Read the access-request article and Cost Management API overview. Credit-request review APIs exist, but no tenant setting for who may request access was documented.

claims.claim: The access-request setting requires the Global administrator role.
claims.quote: To configure the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you need to be assigned to the Global administrator role.

claims.claim: Changes to the access-request setting may take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: Changes to this setting might take up to 24 hours to apply.

claims.claim: The access-request setting does not complete UBB setup by itself.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself.

claims.claim: The printed Anthropic access path follows the cited Claude opt-in procedure, including View all, the subprocessor page and Anthropic selection.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings > View all. ... Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. ... under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences

claims.claim: No documented API equivalent was found for the Anthropic provider user-access setting.
claims.quote: Searched Learn: 'Microsoft Graph Anthropic subprocessor settings access API Copilot', 'Anthropic subprocessor PowerShell'. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor, copilot-anthropic-apps and the returned Graph/provider results; none documented an equivalent tenant provider-access operation.

claims.claim: Claude opt-in requires the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: The Anthropic subprocessor setting governs Claude models rather than GPT-6 Astra.
claims.quote: You can restrict user access to AI provider subprocessors by assigning permissions to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID security groups in the Microsoft 365 admin center. These assignments are applied at the provider level

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude models in the named Microsoft offerings are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary

claims.claim: Claude models are also currently excluded from in-country processing commitments when applicable.
claims.quote: currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Microsoft Product Terms and DPA apply when Claude is provided through Microsoft's subprocessor offering, except the separately labelled Data Retention models.
claims.quote: Unless models are labeled "Anthropic models with Data Retention," the Microsoft Product Terms and Microsoft Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply to the use of Claude models from Anthropic through Microsoft's enterprise Online Services.

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default.
claims.quote: Anthropic models with Data Retention (such as Fable 5.0) have additional controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center and are off by default for all scenarios

claims.claim: Models labelled Anthropic models with Data Retention require separate explicit tenant administrator enablement.
claims.quote: No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anthropic's own terms apply to models with Data Retention.
claims.quote: Anthropic acts as an independent processor and use of Anthropic models with Data Retention is subject to acceptance of Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service and Anthropic's Data Protection Addendum.

claims.claim: Fable-class terms can vary by model and organizational eligibility, so Fable 5.1 cannot simply be treated as sharing every other Fable model's terms.
claims.quote: for certain organizations, Fable 5.1 is available with Anthropic acting as a subprocessor and Microsoft's Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply. ... Other Fable-class models may be provided as "Anthropic models with Data Retention"

claims.claim: Administrators reach Credit requests through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > Top Actions > View requests.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Overview tab. ... From the Top Actions section, you can View requests ... To view and approve credit requests from end users, select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.

claims.claim: The checked sources do not explicitly connect requests from this Chat model-selector rollout to the existing Credit requests page.
claims.quote: Searched: 'model selector UBB government credits request'; read MC1519122, USL/UBB and Monitor Copilot Credit spending. The notice plans later requests; Learn documents general service credit requests without identifying this model-selector integration.

claims.claim: Requests not matching a custom request policy continue through Microsoft's credit request service and can be resolved in the admin center.
claims.quote: Requests that don't match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Dashboard totals are expressed in credits rather than currency.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency.
claims.fix: Replace 'expressed in credits, not currency; finance needs a translation to spend' with 'described as credits-only in the comparison article, while the monitoring article also documents estimated cost in local currency, including negotiated rates; those estimates might not match the bill'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending alongside the comparison article. That article states: 'Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates.'

claims.claim: Dashboard totals are point-in-time views.
claims.quote: Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.
claims.fix: Replace 'Dashboard totals are point-in-time' with 'The comparison article says dashboard totals and exports may be point-in-time views; the monitoring article distinguishes point-in-time exports from dashboard views that continue retrieving live data'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending, which states: 'Exported reports are generated as a point-in-time snapshot, while dashboard views continue to retrieve live data.'

claims.claim: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing discovery setting is deprecated.
claims.quote: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing setting is deprecated.

claims.claim: The deprecated discovery setting controls visibility while Copilot Cost Management controls access and spending.
claims.quote: this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending. Usage-based billing setup overrides discovery for the specified users that you enable usage-based billing for.

claims.claim: Choosing No users in the access-request setting prevents spending-policy requests rather than hiding or blocking UBB model access.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself. ... No users: Users cannot request a spending policy. Instead, they'll be presented with a link to learn more

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges for the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Use Azure Cost Management and Azure billing views to understand billed charges for the Azure subscription connected to your billing method. ... Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows P3 purchase or amortized cost information.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3) and Microsoft Agent pre-purchase plans (P3).

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management does not show prepaid capacity pack consumption, which is monitored in Microsoft 365 or Power Platform admin centers.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management doesn't show consumption against Prepaid Capacity packs. Use the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center, as applicable, to monitor Prepaid Capacity Pack credit usage.

claims.claim: No government-cloud rollout dates for this UBB model-selector item were found.
claims.quote: Searched Learn: '571400 GCC', 'model selector UBB government credits request'. Read the roadmap record, MC1519122 and Anthropic non-federal GCC search excerpts. None gives government rollout dates for UBB models under this item; general Claude GCC availability is a different fact.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The checked sources do not establish how this selector displays metered choices to users without UBB access or whether administrators can hide them.
claims.quote: Searched Learn: 'copilot model selector credits hide'. Read model-selection overview excerpts, discovery setting, access-request setting, and MC1519122. None describes Chat UBB selector visibility for users lacking access; Cowork model-template controls are explicitly Cowork-only.

claims.claim: Per-model spending limits for this Chat selector remain undocumented in the checked material.
claims.quote: Searched Learn: 'copilot Chat per-model limits usage billing'. Read manage-credit and setup articles, Cost Management API overview, and returned usage-limit excerpts. They document policy/per-user limits; model templates are Cowork-only, not Chat per-model spending caps.

claims.claim: Spending policies can automatically include future supported services, and administrators can disable that behavior.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy. ... When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included.

claims.claim: Subscription-covered model choices already exist alongside the newly planned UBB choices.
claims.quote: Model selection is also part of the USL, with some models included with fair use, such as GPT 5.6 and Sonnet, and others included with limits, such as Opus.
